tagline: The second-largest Princes' Island — forested hills, naval history, a magical seminary, and a gentler pace than Büyükada.

items.name: İskele Kafesi
items.description: The café at the ferry landing with views of arriving boats and the harbour. The perfect start to an island day.

items.name: Merit Halki Palace Restoranı
items.description: The restaurant of the historic Heybeliada Palace hotel, with a garden terrace and sea views. Good quality in a beautiful setting.

items.name: Ada Balık Restoranları
items.description: Simple fish restaurants near the harbour serving fresh catch. Quieter and less touristy than Büyükada equivalents.

items.name: Heybeliada Deniz Harp Okulu
items.description: The Turkish Naval Academy occupies a dramatic hilltop on the island. The exterior and surroundings are worth exploring.

items.name: Aya Triada Manastırı (Halki Seminary)
items.description: A beautiful Greek Orthodox seminary on the island's highest hill — closed for decades but historically significant. The hilltop walk is stunning.
items.tip: The walk up through pine forest takes about 40 minutes. Go in the morning for the best views and cool air.

items.name: Island Cycling
items.description: Rent a bicycle at the landing and explore the island's pine-forested roads. Smaller than Büyükada but more varied terrain.
items.tip: The south hill circuit is the best route — takes about 90 minutes at a relaxed pace.

tips: Ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı — Heybeliada is the third stop after Kınalıada and Burgazada.
Much quieter than Büyükada even on summer weekends. A more relaxed island experience.
No cars allowed. Bicycles and horse carriages only.
The island's pine forest is genuinely beautiful. Bring good walking shoes.
